text:
Benji Okafor: Kicking off migration plan discussion for beta rollout schema -> v2 (GA). Need alignment on: compat behavior (read/write), data backfill, and Console messaging for existing beta users. @Jordan Lee @Ethan Park @Chloe Martin @Dylan Brooks @Paula Mendes

Jordan Lee: thx. quick summary of where we landed in PR draft: 
- canonical stored form = rollout_policy_v2 only
- control plane can *ingest* beta fields for a window (feature flag), but will convert to v2 at persistence boundary
- reads will always return v2; we can optionally include `legacy_beta` block for debugging (NOT for public API)

Ethan Park: +1 on “stored v2 only”. We want deterministic eval and fewer branches in policy engine. But we need to be careful about existing beta rollouts in prod DB that are still v1-ish.

Chloe Martin: from Console perspective: we have customers who created beta rollouts via the old UI + some via API. If reads return only v2, old Console clients might break. Are we still gating GA UI behind flag? If yes, we can require upgrade for anyone to even see rollouts.

Dylan Brooks: Console is behind `hosted_rollouts_ga` for now. But existing beta users already have access to beta UI (different flag path). If we flip them to GA UI, they will hit v2 responses.

Paula Mendes: product needs a clean story for beta users: “your existing rollouts continue working; when you edit, we’ll upgrade you to GA schema”. Also want messaging around guardrails being required (we don’t want 100% candidate w/o any thresholds).

Michael Nguyen: re DB: currently we have ~N rollouts with `rollout_policy_json` containing beta keys (weights + optional stickiness bool + guardrails loose). Proposed migration:
1) read-time migration in service layer (if payload has v1 keys, map to v2 struct)
2) background backfill job that rewrites v2 canonical JSON for all existing records (idempotent)
3) after backfill, remove read-time migration branch (later)

Kaitlyn Nguyen: RBAC/entitlements angle: if we “auto-upgrade on edit” we need to ensure permissions don’t accidentally broaden. i.e. user who could edit beta rollouts shouldn’t get to create GA rollouts if their org isn’t entitled.

Jordan Lee: good call. maybe policy is: 
- evaluation path always supports both formats *temporarily*
- update endpoints require GA entitlement when request contains v2 fields OR when endpoint is GA-only
- BUT existing beta rollouts should remain editable for beta-entitled orgs during transition

Marissa Cole: +1. can we define two states:
A) org has beta entitlement only -> can edit beta rollouts; edits stay in compat mode, but we warn
B) org has GA entitlement -> edits result in v2 canonical + guardrails enforcement
We need to avoid blocking existing customers during GA ramp.

Ethan Park: I’m a bit worried about “edits stay in compat mode”. We’ll carry legacy behavior longer. Could we instead always persist v2, but relax validation for migrated beta rollouts unless they opt-in to GA?

Kenji Nakamura: UX idea: show a banner on existing beta rollouts: “This rollout uses beta config. Upgrade to GA to access schedules, guardrails, and audit history.” Two buttons: [Upgrade] [Dismiss]. If they dismiss, they can still view but editing triggers a confirmation modal.

Dylan Brooks: that works. We should also handle the case where they click edit and they’re *not* GA entitled: disable save, show “Contact support to enable GA rollouts.”

Chloe Martin: +1. Also need to decide if “upgrade” is a separate API call or just happens as part of update. I’d prefer explicit `POST /rollouts/:id/upgrade` so we can do strict validation + audit event.

Jordan Lee: explicit upgrade endpoint is nice for audit logs too. We can capture before/after diff cleanly.

Logan Wright: telemetry question: during migration, do we expect variant labels to change? We need stable `variant=baseline|candidate` for metrics. If some beta rollouts used `primary|canary` or arbitrary names, we should normalize.

Michael Nguyen: beta schema today stores `baseline_model` and `candidate_model` but labels are inconsistent in some metrics tags. In v2 we standardize to baseline/candidate. Migration can map any old tags to baseline/candidate, but that means dashboards will show a step change.

Paula Mendes: I’m ok with the step change as long as we message it internally + in release notes. For customers, they mostly just care that compare charts work.

Ethan Park: backfill mechanics:
- batch scan rollouts table by `created_at`
- for each record: parse JSON; if v2 -> noop; if v1 -> convert + write new JSON + set `schema_version=v2` (or embed version field)
- write should be conditional on `updated_at` (optimistic lock) so we don’t clobber concurrent edits

Benji Okafor: what do we do with invalid beta configs? we’ve seen some that don’t sum exactly 100 due to float rounding or 99/1 etc.

Jordan Lee: tolerance: accept sums in [99.9, 100.1] and normalize to ints. If genuinely invalid (e.g. missing candidate), mark rollout `needs_attention` and don’t auto-upgrade; keep evaluating with legacy parser, but UI shows warning.

Dylan Brooks: we need a UI state for that: “This rollout can’t be upgraded automatically due to invalid config. Please recreate rollout or contact support.”

Kaitlyn Nguyen: and ensure only admins see the “contact support” details; normal editors just see “upgrade blocked”.

Chloe Martin: API behavior proposal:
- GET /rollouts/:id returns:
  - `policy_v2` always (best-effort from migration)
  - `migration_status`: `native_v2` | `migrated_preview` | `blocked_invalid`
- PATCH /rollouts/:id:
  - if `migration_status=blocked_invalid` -> 409 with actionable error
  - if org not GA entitled -> allow updates only through legacy beta endpoints (if we keep them), otherwise 403

Marissa Cole: can we avoid exposing `migration_status` publicly? could be internal only? But Console needs it.

Jordan Lee: we can keep it as an internal field behind `X-Redwood-Console` header. For external public API (if any), we don’t promise it.

Ethan Park: I’d rather not have special header logic long-term but ok as a temporary bridge.

Logan Wright: re cardinality: don’t introduce per-rollout migration status tag in metrics. pls no.

Benji Okafor: lol yes. no metric dimension.

Kenji Nakamura: copy suggestions for banner:
- Title: “Upgrade this rollout to GA”
- Body: “Your rollout was created with the beta schema. Upgrading enables guardrails, schedules, and improved audit history.”
- Secondary: “Existing traffic splitting will continue unchanged.”

Paula Mendes: also need an FAQ blurb: “Will upgrading change my current % split?” Answer: no, effective routing remains identical; only schema representation changes + you may be prompted to add guardrails depending on policy.

Jordan Lee: guardrails enforcement nuance: for GA we require at least one of (error_rate OR p95_latency OR token_cost_delta) AND max candidate percent step <= 50 unless admin override. Beta rollouts may violate this. So upgrade flow should either:
- (a) require adding guardrails as part of upgrade, OR
- (b) allow upgrade with “grandfathered” flag but block increasing traffic until guardrails added

Ethan Park: I like (b). Keep routing stable, but prevent riskier actions. Implement as validation rule: if `grandfathered=true` then allow current weights; disallow PATCH that increases candidate_weight above current.

Chloe Martin: from UI: we can lock the traffic slider with tooltip “Add guardrails to increase candidate traffic.”

Dylan Brooks: works. We’ll need API error codes for “grandfathered_limit_exceeded”.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: and ensure admins can override if they have `rollouts.override_guardrails` permission (enterprise only). We should wire that into RBAC bundle.

Michael Nguyen: backfill job should NOT set grandfathered automatically unless config is missing required guardrails. If it already has valid thresholds, it upgrades clean.

Benji Okafor: timeline: can we do backfill before we flip any customers to GA UI?

Ethan Park: yes. we can run backfill in dry-run first (log diffs), then run write mode. Target: end of week.

Jordan Lee: action items:
- @Michael Nguyen draft backfill job plan + safety checks (optimistic lock, rate limiting)
- @Chloe Martin/@Dylan Brooks define API contract for migration_status + upgrade endpoint (internal)
- @Kenji Nakamura finalize banner + blocked-invalid states
- @Kaitlyn Nguyen propose RBAC rules for upgrade vs edit vs override
- I’ll update ADR / migration section in policy schema doc

Paula Mendes: pls include comms plan: beta customers get a heads-up in Console + email? (product will own). Need a clear deprecation date for beta schema.

Benji Okafor: what’s reasonable? 60 days post-GA to stop accepting beta writes?

Ethan Park: 90 days for writes, but reads can be indefinite if we store v2. The key is ingestion. Once everything is v2 in DB, beta ingestion is only needed for any straggler clients.

Dylan Brooks: if we control Console, we can drop beta ingestion sooner. The only risk is customers who scripted against beta endpoints.

Marissa Cole: we’ll set expectation: beta endpoints deprecated 90 days after GA. If any customer is using it, we’ll notify + provide migration guide.

Jordan Lee: cool. I’ll document: “accept beta schema writes until GA+90d; after that return 410 with link to docs.”

(DeployBot): Deploy scheduled: rollout-control-plane canary (policy-migration) -> staging at 2024-10-13 20:30 UTC

Benji Okafor: :thumbsup: thx all. I’ll start a short doc in confluence w/ these decisions and link here.

Chloe Martin: pls tag me when doc is up; I want to make sure API/Console story is consistent.

Kenji Nakamura: same, will drop draft copy in thread when ready.

Logan Wright: and loop me when we decide on metric label normalization so I can update dashboards queries.
